"There was a king among those before you, and he had a sorcerer. When the sorcerer grew old, he said to the king: 'I have grown old, so send me a boy to teach him sorcery.' So he sent him a boy to teach. On his way there was a monk, and the boy sat with him and heard his speech, and it pleased him. Whenever he came to the sorcerer, the sorcerer beat him, and whenever he returned from the sorcerer, he sat with the monk and heard his speech. When he came to his family, they beat him. He complained of this to the monk, who said: 'If you are detained by the sorcerer, say: "My family detained me." And if you are detained by your family, say: "The sorcerer detained me."' While he was in that state, he came upon a huge beast that had blocked the people. He said: 'Today I will know whether the sorcerer or the monk is better.' He took a stone and said: 'O Allah, if the affair of the monk is more beloved to You than the affair of the sorcerer, then kill this beast so the people may pass.' He threw it and killed it, and the people passed. He came to the monk and informed him. The monk said: 'My son, you are today better than me. Your affair has reached what I see, and you will be tested. When you are tested, do not point to me.' The boy used to heal the blind and the leper and treat people for all other ailments. A companion of the king, who had been blind, heard of him and brought him many gifts, saying: 'All this is yours if you cure me.' He said: 'I do not cure anyone; it is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who cures. If you believe in Allah, I will supplicate Allah, and He will cure you.' So he believed in Allah, and Allah cured him. He came to the king walking and sat with him as he used to sit. The king said to him, and asked him: 'By what were you cured?' He said: 'By the supplication of the boy.' So the king sent for the boy and said: 'My son, your sorcery has reached the point that you cure the blind and the leper, and you do such and such.' He continued to torture him until he pointed to the monk. The monk was brought, and it was said to him: 'Return from your religion.' He refused. So he called for a saw, placed the saw at the parting of his head, and sawed him until his two halves fell. Then the boy was brought, and it was said to him: 'Return from your religion.' He refused. So he handed him over to a group of his companions and said to them: 'Take him to such-and-such mountain, climb with him, and when he reaches its peak, if he returns from his religion, well; otherwise, throw him down.' They took him, climbed the mountain with him, and he said: 'O Allah, suffice me against them however You wish.' The mountain shook beneath them and they fell. He came walking to the king, who said to him: 'What did your companions do?' He said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sufficed me against them.' So he handed him over to another group of his companions and said: 'Carry him in a small boat, take him to the middle of the sea, and if he returns from his religion, well; otherwise, cast him into it.'

They took him, and he said: 'O Allah, suffice me against them by whatever You wish.' The boat capsized with them, and they drowned. He came walking to the king, who said to him: 'What did your companions do?' He said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sufficed me against them.' Then he said to the king: 'You will not kill me until you do what I command you.' He said: 'What is it?' He said: 'Gather the people on one level plain, crucify me on a trunk, then take an arrow from my quiver, place the arrow in the middle of the bow, and say: "In the name of Allah, Lord of the boy," then shoot me. When you do that, you will kill me.' So he gathered the people on one level plain, crucified him on a trunk, took an arrow from his quiver, and placed the arrow at his temple. The boy placed his hand at the spot of the arrow and died. The people said:

'We believe in the Lord of the boy, we believe in the Lord of the boy,' three times each.

Then the king was approached and it was said to him: 'You have seen what you were wary of; by Allah, your wariness has come upon you. All the people have believed.' So he ordered [the digging of] the trench at the mouths of the streets, lit the fires, and said: 'Whoever does not return from his religion, throw him into it,' or it was said to him: 'Leap in.' They did that, until a woman came with a small child of hers, and she hesitated to fall into it. The boy said: 'O mother, be patient, for you are upon the truth.'" [122] [[Al-Ahad wa al-Mathani by al-Dahhak: 1/219–221, no. 187; and Sahih Muslim: 8/231.]]

Muhammad ibn Yahya said: Muslim ibn Qutayba narrated to us, who said: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from Ayyub, from ʿIkrima, concerning the saying of Allah, Glorified be He: ﴿Qutila ashab al-ukhdud﴾ (Cursed were the people of the trench). He said: "They were from your people, the Nabat." Al-Kalbi said: "They were Christians of Najran. The king of Najran seized believing people there, dug seven trenches for them in the ground, each forty cubits long and twelve cubits wide, then cast into them [naft] [[As in the manuscript.]] and firewood, then presented them to it. Whoever refused, they threw into the fire." He began with a man called ʿAmr ibn Zayd, and their king asked him: "Who taught you this?" meaning the tawhid (affirmation of Allah's oneness). He refused to tell him. So they brought the one who had taught him tawhid and said: "O king, I taught him." His name was ʿAbd Allah ibn Shamir, and he was thrown into the fire. Then they presented the believers to the fire one by one, until when he wanted to take the rest of the believers, their king made an idol of gold and appointed over every ten believers a man who would say to them: "When you hear the sound of the flutes, prostrate to the idol. Whoever does not prostrate, throw him into the fire." When the Christians heard of this, they prostrated to the idol, but the believers refused. So he dug trenches for them and threw them in, and the fire rose above them twelve cubits.

Muqatil said: "The trenches were three: one in Najran in Yemen, another in Syria, and another in Persia, where they were burned with fire. As for the one in Syria, it was Antiochus ibn Maysar the Roman; as for the one in Persia, it was Bukhtnassar; and as for the one in the land of the Arabs, it was Yusuf ibn Dhi Nuwas. Allah did not send down a Qur'an concerning those in Persia and Syria, but He sent down concerning the one in Najran. That was because two Muslim men, of those who read the Gospel, one in the land of Tihama and the other in Najran of Yemen, one of them hired himself out for a job and began reading the Gospel. The daughter of his employer saw a light shining while he was reading the Gospel, and she told her father of it. He watched him until he saw it, and asked him, but he did not inform him. He kept at him until he informed him of the religion and Islam. So he (the employer) and eighty-seven persons, men and women, followed him, and this was after ʿIsa had been raised to heaven. Yusuf ibn Dhi Nuwas ibn Sharahil ibn Tubba' ibn al-Yasuh al-Himyari heard of that, dug trenches for them in the ground, lit fires in them, and presented them with disbelief. Whoever refused to disbelieve, he threw into the fire, and whoever returned from the religion of ʿIsa was not thrown into the fire. A woman came with a small child who could not speak. When she stood at the edge of the trench, she looked at her son and drew back from the fire. She was struck until she moved forward, and she continued like that three times. When it was the third time, she went to turn back, and her son said to her: 'O mother, I see before you a fire that will not be extinguished.' When she heard her son say that, they both threw themselves into the fire together, and Allah made her and her son to be in Paradise. On that single day, seventy-seven persons were thrown into the fire."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Whoever refused to fall into the fire was beaten with whips, and their spirits were admitted into Paradise before their bodies reached the fire."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih that a man who had remained upon the religion of ʿIsa came to Najran and invited them, and they answered him. Dhu Nuwas the Jew marched against him with troops from Himyar and gave them the choice between the fire and Judaism. They refused him, so he dug the trenches and burned twelve thousand. Al-Kalbi said: "The People of the Trench were seventy thousand."

Wahb said: "When Abraha overcame Yemen, Dhu Nuwas fled and plunged into the sea with his horse, and drowned." In this regard ʿAmr ibn Maʿdi Karib said:

"You threaten me as if you were Dhu Ruʿayn,
or Dhu Nuwas in his most pleasant life.
Before you there were blessings and a kingdom firmly established among people,
ancient its covenant, from whose covenant was ʿAd,
great, conqueror of tyranny, harsh.
Time removed their kingship, and it became
transferred among people from people."

Al-Kalbi said: "Dhu Nuwas is the one who killed ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Tamir, and the story has already passed in the raised (marfuʿ) hadith to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Something that makes it clearer is what ʿAta' narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he said: "In Najran there was a king from the kings of Himyar called Yusuf Dhu Nuwas ibn Sharahbil ibn Sharahil, in the interval before the birth of the Prophet (ﷺ) by ninety years."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Muhammad ibn Bahir narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Humayd al-Kashshi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, who said: Yaʿqub ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Qummi narrated to us, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Abi al-Mughira narrated to us, from Ibn [Abzi], who said: "When the Muslims defeated the people of Isfandhan, they turned back, and he (ʿUmar) came to them, and they gathered. They said: 'What rulings apply to the Magians? They are not People of the Book, nor are they among the polytheist Arabs.' ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said: 'Rather, they are People of the Book, and they were adhering to their scripture. Wine had been made lawful for them. A king of theirs took it and it overpowered his mind, so he had relations with his sister. When the intoxication left him, he regretted and said to her: "Woe to you, what is this that I have done, and what is the way out of it?"

She said: "The way out is that you address the people, saying: 'O people, Allah has made lawful the marriage of sisters.' When it has departed from the people and they forget it, then you address them and forbid it."

So he stood as a preacher and said: "O people, Allah has made lawful the marriage of sisters." The people, all of them, said: "God forbid that we believe in this or acknowledge it. No prophet has brought it to us, nor was it sent down to us in a book." He returned to his partner and said: "Woe to you, the people have refused me." She said: "If they refuse you, then spread the whip among them." He said: "So he spread the whip among them, but the people refused to acknowledge it." He returned to her and said: "I have spread the whip among them, and they refused to acknowledge it." She said: "Then draw the sword against them." He said: "So he drew the sword against them, but they refused to acknowledge it." He said to her: "Woe to you, the people have refused to acknowledge it." She said: "Dig for them a trench, then light fires in it, then present to it the people of your kingdom. Whoever follows you, leave him alone; and whoever refuses, throw him into the fire." So he dug a trench for them, lit fires in it, and presented the people of his realm to that. Whoever refused was thrown into the fire, and whoever agreed was let go." So Allah, Glorified be He, sent down concerning them: ﴿Qutila ashab al-ukhdud. The fire full of fuel﴾ up to His saying: ﴿ʿadhab al-hariq﴾ (the punishment of the burning) [[Tafsir al-Tabari with slight variation: 30/166.]].

Al-Dahhak said: "The People of the Trench were from the Children of Israel. They seized men and women, dug a trench for them, then lit fires in it and made the believers stand over it, saying: 'Will you disbelieve, or shall we throw you into the fire?' They claim that they were Daniel and his companions." This is the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, who said: ʿUmar ibn Muhammad ibn Bahir narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Yunus, from Shayban, from Qatada, concerning the saying of Allah, Glorified be He: ﴿Qutila ashab al-ukhdud﴾. He said: "[Someone] narrated to us that ʿAli ibn Abi Talib used to say: 'They were people in Mudra' of Yemen. Their believers fought their disbelievers, and the believers prevailed over the disbelievers. Then they fought a second time, and the believers prevailed over the disbelievers. Then they took covenants and pledges from one another that none would betray another. But their disbelievers betrayed them and seized them. Then a man from among the believers said to them: "Is there for you some good? Kindle a fire, then present us to it. Whoever follows you in your religion, that is what you desire; and whoever does not, let him leap into the fire, and you will be rid of him." So they kindled a fire and presented them to it, and they began to leap into it, until only an old woman remained, as if she hesitated. A small child in her lap said to her: "Go on, and do not hesitate." So Allah related to them their news and their story."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid also informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Muzani informed us, who said: Mutayn narrated to us, who said: ʿUthman narrated to us, who said: Muʿawiya ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Sharik, from Jabir, from Abu al-Tufayl, from ʿAli, who said: "The People of the Trench, their prophet was Abyssinian." ʿAli said: "A prophet from Abyssinia was sent to his people." Then he recited to me: ﴿Wa-laqad arsalna rusulan min qablika minhum man qasasna ʿalayka wa-minhum man lam naqsus ʿalayka﴾ (And We certainly sent messengers before you; of them are those We have related to you, and of them are those We have not related to you) [[Surah Ghafir 40:78.]]. The prophet invited them, and some people followed him. They fought them, and his companions were killed, and he was seized and bound, but he escaped from them. They dug a trench and filled it with fire. Whoever followed the prophet was thrown into it, and whoever followed them was left alone. Then they brought a woman with a suckling child, and she recoiled. He said: "O mother, go on and do not hesitate." [[The same source, in which: "go on and do not wail."]]

And through him, from Mutayn, who said: Abu Musa narrated to us, and he said: "In their land there was a boy called ʿAbd Allah ibn Tamir. His father had handed him over to a teacher to teach him sorcery. The boy disliked that and found no escape from obeying his father, so he kept going to the teacher. On his way there was a monk of beautiful recitation and beautiful voice, which pleased him. He would come to the teacher after the other boys, and the teacher would beat him, saying: 'What detained you?' When he returned to his father, he entered upon the monk, and his father beat him, saying: 'Why were you late?' So the boy complained of this to the monk, who said to him: 'When you come to the teacher, say: "My father detained me." And when you come to your father, say: "The teacher detained me."'

In that land there was a huge serpent that cut off the road for the people. The boy passed by it, threw at it, and killed it. The monk learned of this and was all the more amazed by him, and said: 'You killed it?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'You have a great affair.'

The king had a son who was blind. He heard about the boy and that he had killed the serpent, so he came to him with an attendant and said: 'Did you kill the serpent?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Who killed it?' He said: 'Allah.' He said: 'Who is Allah?' He said: 'Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and Lord of the sun, the moon, the night and the day, and this world and the Hereafter.' He said: 'If you are truthful, then supplicate your Lord that He return my sight to me.' The boy said: 'Do you see? If Allah returns your sight to you, will you believe in Him?' He said: 'Yes.' The boy said: 'O Allah, if he is truthful, return his sight to him.' Allah, Exalted, returned his sight to him, and he went back to his home without an attendant. Then he entered upon the king, and when the king saw him, he was amazed and said: 'Who did this?' He said: 'Allah.' He said: 'And who is Allah?' He said: 'Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, Lord of the East and the West, Lord of the sun, the moon, the night and the day, and this world and the Hereafter.' The king said to him: 'Tell me, who taught you this?' and he pointed to the boy. He called him and spoke with him, and he was an intelligent boy. He asked him about his religion, and the boy informed him of Islam and of those who believed with him. The king resolved to kill them, fearing that they would change his religion. So he sent them to the top of a mountain and said: 'Throw them from the top of the mountain.' They took the boy to the highest mountain, and the boy supplicated his Lord, and Allah destroyed them. This angered the king. Then he sent men with them to the sea and said: 'Drown them.' The boy supplicated his Lord, and He drowned them, and he and his companions were saved. He entered upon the king, who said: 'What did your companions do, those whom I sent with you?' He said: 'Allah destroyed them and saved me.' He said: 'Kill him with the sword.' But the sword turned away from him. His news spread in the land of Yemen, and people knew him and magnified him, and they knew that he and his companions were upon the truth. The boy said to the king: 'You will not be able to kill me unless you do what I tell you.' He said: 'How shall I kill you?' He said: 'Gather the people of your kingdom while you are on your throne, then shoot me with an arrow in the name of my God.' The king did so, then he shot him in the name of the boy's God, and it struck him and killed him. The people said:"

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 85, verse 4–22 (part 2 of 2):

There is no god but Allah, the Lord of Abdullah ibn Thamir, and there is no religion but his religion." The king became angry, closed the door, seized the mouths of the lanes, and dug a trench (ukhdud) and filled it with fire. Then he presented them to himself man by man: whoever turned back from Islam he left alone, and whoever said, "My religion is the religion of Abdullah," he threw into the trench and burned him. In his kingdom there was a woman who had embraced Islam along with those who embraced it, and she had three children, one of whom was an infant. The king said to her, "Return from your religion, or I will throw you into the fire and your children with you." She refused, so he took her eldest son and threw him into the fire. Then he said to her, "Return to your religion," and she refused, so he threw the second into the fire. Then he said to her, "Return from your religion," and she refused. They took the child from her to throw him into the fire, and the woman was about to turn back, but the child said, "O mother, do not turn back from Islam, for you are upon the truth and there is no harm upon you." The child was thrown into the fire, and his mother was thrown after him. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾ [[With variation from the tafsir of al-Qurtubi: 19/289.]].

And al-Dahhak said: Bukhtnassar burned a group of the Muslims.

Al-ukhdud: the pit, and the long cleft in the earth like a river; its plural is akhadid. It is on the pattern of af'ul from al-khadd; one says "khaddadtu fi al-ard khaddan," meaning I cut and dug.

﴿The fire fueled with wood﴾: the common reading is with a fatha on the waw, meaning the fuel (al-khatb). Abu Raja' al-Utaridi read it with a damma on the waw, as a verbal noun (masdar). The common reading of ﴿nari dhat﴾ is with a kasra, so both are in apposition (na't) to al-ukhdud. Ashhab al-Uqayli read it with a raf' in both, meaning: ﴿the fire fueled with wood﴾ burned them.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The people of the trench were a group of believers who had withdrawn from people during a period of interruption (fatra). A tyrant of the idol-worshippers sent for them and invited them to enter his religion, but they refused. So he dug a trench, kindled a fire in it, and gave them the choice between entering his religion and being thrown into the fire. They chose being thrown into the fire over returning from their religion, and they were thrown in. Allah saved the believers who were thrown into the fire by taking their souls before the fire touched them, and the fire came out upon those of the disbelievers who were on the edge of the trench and burned them.

﴿While they sat over it, and they were witnesses to what they did to the believers﴾: witnesses, present. Muqatil said: meaning they bear witness that the believers, when they abandoned the worship of the idol, ﴿and they did not hold it against them﴾: that is, they found no fault in them, found no crime in them, and saw no wrong in them, ﴿except that they believed in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; and Allah is Witness over all things﴾. ﴿except that they believed﴾: meaning, except because and for the reason that they believed.

﴿Indeed, those who afflicted the believing men and believing women﴾: tortured and burned them. Its parallel is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿On the day they will be tried over the Fire﴾ [[Surat al-Dhariyat: 13.]], ﴿then they did not repent, so for them is the punishment of Hell﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and for them is the punishment of burning﴾ in this world. This is because Allah, Exalted is He, burned them with that same fire with which they had burned the believers. This is the statement of al-Rabi' and his companions. Others said: the two are one.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Lu'lu' al-Warraq told us, saying: Abu Ubayd Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Mu'ammal al-Sayrafi told us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Ahwal, known as al-Luqluq, told us, saying: Mansur ibn Ammar told us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Tawba told us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Jahm, traced back to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ confided to me a hadith about the Fire. He said: "O Hudhayfah, in Hell there are lions of fire, dogs of fire, hooks of fire, and swords of fire. Allah will send angels who will hang the people of the Fire by those hooks by their jaws, and cut them with those swords limb by limb, and throw them to those dogs and lions; whenever they cut off a limb, a new limb returns in its place." [123] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/174.]]

﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great triumph.﴾ The scholars differed regarding the response (jawab) of the oath. Some said: its response is ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾, and there is an omission in it, meaning: "Indeed, it was destroyed." It was also said: there is an inversion (taqdim and ta'khir), its intended sense being: ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench, by the sky of the constellations﴾.

Qatadah said: its response is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the seizing of your Lord is severe﴾, meaning His seizing with punishment and vengeance.

﴿Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats﴾: meaning, creation, according to most scholars. Ata al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿He originates﴾ the punishment in this world for the disbelievers, then ﴿repeats﴾ the punishment upon them in the Hereafter.

﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Loving﴾. Ibn Abbas said: His affection (tawaddud) toward His allies through forgiveness. Ali narrated from him: the Beloved. Mujahid: the Loving (al-Wadd). Ibn Zayd: the Merciful. It was also said: it is in the sense of the one loved (al-mawdud), like al-halub and al-rakub. It was also said: its meaning is that He forgives and loves to forgive.

﴿Lord of the Throne, the Glorious﴾: the great throne. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: the Generous. The reciters differed regarding it: Yahya, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read it with a kasra on the dal, as a descriptive (na't) of al-Arsh (the Throne). Others read it with a raf', as an attribute of al-Ghafur.

﴿Doer of what He intends﴾. ﴿Has there reached you the story of the hosts﴾: news of the destroyed armies. Then He specified who they were, saying:

﴿Pharaoh and Thamud﴾. ﴿But those who disbelieve are in denial﴾: from your people, O Muhammad. ﴿[And they submitted to torment]﴾ [[So in the manuscript.]], like the practice of those before them. ﴿And Allah, from behind them, is encompassing﴾: knowing of them, nothing of their conditions being hidden from Him. ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an﴾: noble, honorable, abundant in good, and not as the polytheists claimed. Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya said: "Majid" means uncreated.

Ibn al-Sumayqa read: ﴿Bal huwa Quranu majidin﴾ with idafa, meaning the Qur'an of a glorious Lord.

﴿In a preserved tablet﴾.

Yahya ibn Ya'mur read: ﴿fi luhin﴾ with a damma on the lam, meaning that it is in a tablet, and it is possessed of light, elevation and honor.

The others read it with a fatha on the lam, ﴿lawhin mahfuz﴾. Nafi' and Ibn Mikhzar read the dhal of ﴿mahfuzun﴾ with a damma as a descriptive of the Qur'an; the rest read it with a kasra as a descriptive of the tablet.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Makhlad told us, saying: Ibn Khalawayh told us, saying: Isma'il told us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr told us, saying: Muqatil and Ibn Jurayj informed me, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: At the head of the tablet is: "There is no god but Allah alone; His religion is Islam, and Muhammad is His servant and Messenger." Whoever believes in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, affirms His promise and follows His messengers, He will admit into Paradise. He said: The tablet is of white pearl, its length the distance between the heavens and the earth, its width the distance between east and west; its edges are of pearls and rubies, its covers are of red ruby, its pen is light, and its writing is a decree fastened to the Throne. Its origin is in the lap of an angel called Matriyun, protected from the devils. That is His saying: ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an in a preserved tablet﴾. For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in it, every day, are three hundred and sixty glances: He gives life and causes death, honors and humbles, and ﴿does what He wills﴾.

Aqil informed me that al-Mu'afa informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Amr ibn Ali told us, saying: I heard Qurrah ibn Sulayman say: Harb ibn Surayh told us, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhayb told us, from Anas ibn Malik, regarding His saying: ﴿It is a glorious Qur'an in a preserved tablet﴾. He said: The preserved tablet which Allah mentioned is on the forehead of Israfil. Muqatil said: The preserved tablet is to the right of the Throne.

**Qutila** (was cursed): Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Everything in the Qur'an that uses *qutila* means *la'ana* (was cursed)."

**Ashab al-Ukhdud** (the People of the Trench): *al-Shaqq* (the cleft). The scholars differed about them.

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Jaʿfar informed us, saying: al-Hakim Abu Muhammad Yahya ibn Mansur, and Abu al-Qasim Mansur ibn al-ʿAbbas (the sons of Shanj), and Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Mahmud ibn ʿUbayd Allah in Merv, and Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd Allah al-Tahiri [....] [[An illegible word in the manuscript.]], and the wording is his, said: Al-Hasan ibn Shaybān ibn ʿĀmir al-Shaybani narrated to us that Hudba ibn Khalid al-Qaysi narrated to them, saying: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, and I was told by Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Muhammad ibn Maʿmar narrated to me, who said: Harmi ibn ʿUmara narrated to me, who said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, who said: Thabit ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, from Suhayb, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"There was a king among those before you, and he had a sorcerer. When the sorcerer grew old, he said to the king: 'I have grown old, so send me a boy to teach him sorcery.' So he sent him a boy to teach. On his way there was a monk, and the boy sat with him and heard his speech, and it pleased him. Whenever he came to the sorcerer, the sorcerer beat him, and whenever he returned from the sorcerer, he sat with the monk and heard his speech. When he came to his family, they beat him. He complained of this to the monk, who said: 'If you are detained by the sorcerer, say: "My family detained me." And if you are detained by your family, say: "The sorcerer detained me."' While he was in that state, he came upon a huge beast that had blocked the people. He said: 'Today I will know whether the sorcerer or the monk is better.' He took a stone and said: 'O Allah, if the affair of the monk is more beloved to You than the affair of the sorcerer, then kill this beast so the people may pass.' He threw it and killed it, and the people passed. He came to the monk and informed him. The monk said: 'My son, you are today better than me. Your affair has reached what I see, and you will be tested. When you are tested, do not point to me.' The boy used to heal the blind and the leper and treat people for all other ailments. A companion of the king, who had been blind, heard of him and brought him many gifts, saying: 'All this is yours if you cure me.' He said: 'I do not cure anyone; it is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who cures. If you believe in Allah, I will supplicate Allah, and He will cure you.' So he believed in Allah, and Allah cured him. He came to the king walking and sat with him as he used to sit. The king said to him, and asked him: 'By what were you cured?' He said: 'By the supplication of the boy.' So the king sent for the boy and said: 'My son, your sorcery has reached the point that you cure the blind and the leper, and you do such and such.' He continued to torture him until he pointed to the monk. The monk was brought, and it was said to him: 'Return from your religion.' He refused. So he called for a saw, placed the saw at the parting of his head, and sawed him until his two halves fell. Then the boy was brought, and it was said to him: 'Return from your religion.' He refused. So he handed him over to a group of his companions and said to them: 'Take him to such-and-such mountain, climb with him, and when he reaches its peak, if he returns from his religion, well; otherwise, throw him down.' They took him, climbed the mountain with him, and he said: 'O Allah, suffice me against them however You wish.' The mountain shook beneath them and they fell. He came walking to the king, who said to him: 'What did your companions do?' He said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sufficed me against them.' So he handed him over to another group of his companions and said: 'Carry him in a small boat, take him to the middle of the sea, and if he returns from his religion, well; otherwise, cast him into it.'

They took him, and he said: 'O Allah, suffice me against them by whatever You wish.' The boat capsized with them, and they drowned. He came walking to the king, who said to him: 'What did your companions do?' He said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sufficed me against them.' Then he said to the king: 'You will not kill me until you do what I command you.' He said: 'What is it?' He said: 'Gather the people on one level plain, crucify me on a trunk, then take an arrow from my quiver, place the arrow in the middle of the bow, and say: "In the name of Allah, Lord of the boy," then shoot me. When you do that, you will kill me.' So he gathered the people on one level plain, crucified him on a trunk, took an arrow from his quiver, and placed the arrow at his temple. The boy placed his hand at the spot of the arrow and died. The people said:

'We believe in the Lord of the boy, we believe in the Lord of the boy,' three times each.

Then the king was approached and it was said to him: 'You have seen what you were wary of; by Allah, your wariness has come upon you. All the people have believed.' So he ordered [the digging of] the trench at the mouths of the streets, lit the fires, and said: 'Whoever does not return from his religion, throw him into it,' or it was said to him: 'Leap in.' They did that, until a woman came with a small child of hers, and she hesitated to fall into it. The boy said: 'O mother, be patient, for you are upon the truth.'" [122] [[Al-Ahad wa al-Mathani by al-Dahhak: 1/219–221, no. 187; and Sahih Muslim: 8/231.]]

Muhammad ibn Yahya said: Muslim ibn Qutayba narrated to us, who said: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from Ayyub, from ʿIkrima, concerning the saying of Allah, Glorified be He: ﴿Qutila ashab al-ukhdud﴾ (Cursed were the people of the trench). He said: "They were from your people, the Nabat." Al-Kalbi said: "They were Christians of Najran. The king of Najran seized believing people there, dug seven trenches for them in the ground, each forty cubits long and twelve cubits wide, then cast into them [naft] [[As in the manuscript.]] and firewood, then presented them to it. Whoever refused, they threw into the fire." He began with a man called ʿAmr ibn Zayd, and their king asked him: "Who taught you this?" meaning the tawhid (affirmation of Allah's oneness). He refused to tell him. So they brought the one who had taught him tawhid and said: "O king, I taught him." His name was ʿAbd Allah ibn Shamir, and he was thrown into the fire. Then they presented the believers to the fire one by one, until when he wanted to take the rest of the believers, their king made an idol of gold and appointed over every ten believers a man who would say to them: "When you hear the sound of the flutes, prostrate to the idol. Whoever does not prostrate, throw him into the fire." When the Christians heard of this, they prostrated to the idol, but the believers refused. So he dug trenches for them and threw them in, and the fire rose above them twelve cubits.

Muqatil said: "The trenches were three: one in Najran in Yemen, another in Syria, and another in Persia, where they were burned with fire. As for the one in Syria, it was Antiochus ibn Maysar the Roman; as for the one in Persia, it was Bukhtnassar; and as for the one in the land of the Arabs, it was Yusuf ibn Dhi Nuwas. Allah did not send down a Qur'an concerning those in Persia and Syria, but He sent down concerning the one in Najran. That was because two Muslim men, of those who read the Gospel, one in the land of Tihama and the other in Najran of Yemen, one of them hired himself out for a job and began reading the Gospel. The daughter of his employer saw a light shining while he was reading the Gospel, and she told her father of it. He watched him until he saw it, and asked him, but he did not inform him. He kept at him until he informed him of the religion and Islam. So he (the employer) and eighty-seven persons, men and women, followed him, and this was after ʿIsa had been raised to heaven. Yusuf ibn Dhi Nuwas ibn Sharahil ibn Tubba' ibn al-Yasuh al-Himyari heard of that, dug trenches for them in the ground, lit fires in them, and presented them with disbelief. Whoever refused to disbelieve, he threw into the fire, and whoever returned from the religion of ʿIsa was not thrown into the fire. A woman came with a small child who could not speak. When she stood at the edge of the trench, she looked at her son and drew back from the fire. She was struck until she moved forward, and she continued like that three times. When it was the third time, she went to turn back, and her son said to her: 'O mother, I see before you a fire that will not be extinguished.' When she heard her son say that, they both threw themselves into the fire together, and Allah made her and her son to be in Paradise. On that single day, seventy-seven persons were thrown into the fire."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Whoever refused to fall into the fire was beaten with whips, and their spirits were admitted into Paradise before their bodies reached the fire."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih that a man who had remained upon the religion of ʿIsa came to Najran and invited them, and they answered him. Dhu Nuwas the Jew marched against him with troops from Himyar and gave them the choice between the fire and Judaism. They refused him, so he dug the trenches and burned twelve thousand. Al-Kalbi said: "The People of the Trench were seventy thousand."

Wahb said: "When Abraha overcame Yemen, Dhu Nuwas fled and plunged into the sea with his horse, and drowned." In this regard ʿAmr ibn Maʿdi Karib said:

"You threaten me as if you were Dhu Ruʿayn,
or Dhu Nuwas in his most pleasant life.
Before you there were blessings and a kingdom firmly established among people,
ancient its covenant, from whose covenant was ʿAd,
great, conqueror of tyranny, harsh.
Time removed their kingship, and it became
transferred among people from people."

Al-Kalbi said: "Dhu Nuwas is the one who killed ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Tamir, and the story has already passed in the raised (marfuʿ) hadith to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Something that makes it clearer is what ʿAta' narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he said: "In Najran there was a king from the kings of Himyar called Yusuf Dhu Nuwas ibn Sharahbil ibn Sharahil, in the interval before the birth of the Prophet (ﷺ) by ninety years."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Muhammad ibn Bahir narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Humayd al-Kashshi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, who said: Yaʿqub ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Qummi narrated to us, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Abi al-Mughira narrated to us, from Ibn [Abzi], who said: "When the Muslims defeated the people of Isfandhan, they turned back, and he (ʿUmar) came to them, and they gathered. They said: 'What rulings apply to the Magians? They are not People of the Book, nor are they among the polytheist Arabs.' ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said: 'Rather, they are People of the Book, and they were adhering to their scripture. Wine had been made lawful for them. A king of theirs took it and it overpowered his mind, so he had relations with his sister. When the intoxication left him, he regretted and said to her: "Woe to you, what is this that I have done, and what is the way out of it?"

She said: "The way out is that you address the people, saying: 'O people, Allah has made lawful the marriage of sisters.' When it has departed from the people and they forget it, then you address them and forbid it."

So he stood as a preacher and said: "O people, Allah has made lawful the marriage of sisters." The people, all of them, said: "God forbid that we believe in this or acknowledge it. No prophet has brought it to us, nor was it sent down to us in a book." He returned to his partner and said: "Woe to you, the people have refused me." She said: "If they refuse you, then spread the whip among them." He said: "So he spread the whip among them, but the people refused to acknowledge it." He returned to her and said: "I have spread the whip among them, and they refused to acknowledge it." She said: "Then draw the sword against them." He said: "So he drew the sword against them, but they refused to acknowledge it." He said to her: "Woe to you, the people have refused to acknowledge it." She said: "Dig for them a trench, then light fires in it, then present to it the people of your kingdom. Whoever follows you, leave him alone; and whoever refuses, throw him into the fire." So he dug a trench for them, lit fires in it, and presented the people of his realm to that. Whoever refused was thrown into the fire, and whoever agreed was let go." So Allah, Glorified be He, sent down concerning them: ﴿Qutila ashab al-ukhdud. The fire full of fuel﴾ up to His saying: ﴿ʿadhab al-hariq﴾ (the punishment of the burning) [[Tafsir al-Tabari with slight variation: 30/166.]].

Al-Dahhak said: "The People of the Trench were from the Children of Israel. They seized men and women, dug a trench for them, then lit fires in it and made the believers stand over it, saying: 'Will you disbelieve, or shall we throw you into the fire?' They claim that they were Daniel and his companions." This is the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, who said: ʿUmar ibn Muhammad ibn Bahir narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Yunus, from Shayban, from Qatada, concerning the saying of Allah, Glorified be He: ﴿Qutila ashab al-ukhdud﴾. He said: "[Someone] narrated to us that ʿAli ibn Abi Talib used to say: 'They were people in Mudra' of Yemen. Their believers fought their disbelievers, and the believers prevailed over the disbelievers. Then they fought a second time, and the believers prevailed over the disbelievers. Then they took covenants and pledges from one another that none would betray another. But their disbelievers betrayed them and seized them. Then a man from among the believers said to them: "Is there for you some good? Kindle a fire, then present us to it. Whoever follows you in your religion, that is what you desire; and whoever does not, let him leap into the fire, and you will be rid of him." So they kindled a fire and presented them to it, and they began to leap into it, until only an old woman remained, as if she hesitated. A small child in her lap said to her: "Go on, and do not hesitate." So Allah related to them their news and their story."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid also informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Muzani informed us, who said: Mutayn narrated to us, who said: ʿUthman narrated to us, who said: Muʿawiya ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Sharik, from Jabir, from Abu al-Tufayl, from ʿAli, who said: "The People of the Trench, their prophet was Abyssinian." ʿAli said: "A prophet from Abyssinia was sent to his people." Then he recited to me: ﴿Wa-laqad arsalna rusulan min qablika minhum man qasasna ʿalayka wa-minhum man lam naqsus ʿalayka﴾ (And We certainly sent messengers before you; of them are those We have related to you, and of them are those We have not related to you) [[Surah Ghafir 40:78.]]. The prophet invited them, and some people followed him. They fought them, and his companions were killed, and he was seized and bound, but he escaped from them. They dug a trench and filled it with fire. Whoever followed the prophet was thrown into it, and whoever followed them was left alone. Then they brought a woman with a suckling child, and she recoiled. He said: "O mother, go on and do not hesitate." [[The same source, in which: "go on and do not wail."]]

And through him, from Mutayn, who said: Abu Musa narrated to us, and he said: "In their land there was a boy called ʿAbd Allah ibn Tamir. His father had handed him over to a teacher to teach him sorcery. The boy disliked that and found no escape from obeying his father, so he kept going to the teacher. On his way there was a monk of beautiful recitation and beautiful voice, which pleased him. He would come to the teacher after the other boys, and the teacher would beat him, saying: 'What detained you?' When he returned to his father, he entered upon the monk, and his father beat him, saying: 'Why were you late?' So the boy complained of this to the monk, who said to him: 'When you come to the teacher, say: "My father detained me." And when you come to your father, say: "The teacher detained me."'

In that land there was a huge serpent that cut off the road for the people. The boy passed by it, threw at it, and killed it. The monk learned of this and was all the more amazed by him, and said: 'You killed it?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'You have a great affair.'

The king had a son who was blind. He heard about the boy and that he had killed the serpent, so he came to him with an attendant and said: 'Did you kill the serpent?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Who killed it?' He said: 'Allah.' He said: 'Who is Allah?' He said: 'Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and Lord of the sun, the moon, the night and the day, and this world and the Hereafter.' He said: 'If you are truthful, then supplicate your Lord that He return my sight to me.' The boy said: 'Do you see? If Allah returns your sight to you, will you believe in Him?' He said: 'Yes.' The boy said: 'O Allah, if he is truthful, return his sight to him.' Allah, Exalted, returned his sight to him, and he went back to his home without an attendant. Then he entered upon the king, and when the king saw him, he was amazed and said: 'Who did this?' He said: 'Allah.' He said: 'And who is Allah?' He said: 'Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, Lord of the East and the West, Lord of the sun, the moon, the night and the day, and this world and the Hereafter.' The king said to him: 'Tell me, who taught you this?' and he pointed to the boy. He called him and spoke with him, and he was an intelligent boy. He asked him about his religion, and the boy informed him of Islam and of those who believed with him. The king resolved to kill them, fearing that they would change his religion. So he sent them to the top of a mountain and said: 'Throw them from the top of the mountain.' They took the boy to the highest mountain, and the boy supplicated his Lord, and Allah destroyed them. This angered the king. Then he sent men with them to the sea and said: 'Drown them.' The boy supplicated his Lord, and He drowned them, and he and his companions were saved. He entered upon the king, who said: 'What did your companions do, those whom I sent with you?' He said: 'Allah destroyed them and saved me.' He said: 'Kill him with the sword.' But the sword turned away from him. His news spread in the land of Yemen, and people knew him and magnified him, and they knew that he and his companions were upon the truth. The boy said to the king: 'You will not be able to kill me unless you do what I tell you.' He said: 'How shall I kill you?' He said: 'Gather the people of your kingdom while you are on your throne, then shoot me with an arrow in the name of my God.' The king did so, then he shot him in the name of the boy's God, and it struck him and killed him. The people said:"

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 85, verse 4–22 (part 2 of 2):

There is no god but Allah, the Lord of Abdullah ibn Thamir, and there is no religion but his religion." The king became angry, closed the door, seized the mouths of the lanes, and dug a trench (ukhdud) and filled it with fire. Then he presented them to himself man by man: whoever turned back from Islam he left alone, and whoever said, "My religion is the religion of Abdullah," he threw into the trench and burned him. In his kingdom there was a woman who had embraced Islam along with those who embraced it, and she had three children, one of whom was an infant. The king said to her, "Return from your religion, or I will throw you into the fire and your children with you." She refused, so he took her eldest son and threw him into the fire. Then he said to her, "Return to your religion," and she refused, so he threw the second into the fire. Then he said to her, "Return from your religion," and she refused. They took the child from her to throw him into the fire, and the woman was about to turn back, but the child said, "O mother, do not turn back from Islam, for you are upon the truth and there is no harm upon you." The child was thrown into the fire, and his mother was thrown after him. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾ [[With variation from the tafsir of al-Qurtubi: 19/289.]].

And al-Dahhak said: Bukhtnassar burned a group of the Muslims.

Al-ukhdud: the pit, and the long cleft in the earth like a river; its plural is akhadid. It is on the pattern of af'ul from al-khadd; one says "khaddadtu fi al-ard khaddan," meaning I cut and dug.

﴿The fire fueled with wood﴾: the common reading is with a fatha on the waw, meaning the fuel (al-khatb). Abu Raja' al-Utaridi read it with a damma on the waw, as a verbal noun (masdar). The common reading of ﴿nari dhat﴾ is with a kasra, so both are in apposition (na't) to al-ukhdud. Ashhab al-Uqayli read it with a raf' in both, meaning: ﴿the fire fueled with wood﴾ burned them.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The people of the trench were a group of believers who had withdrawn from people during a period of interruption (fatra). A tyrant of the idol-worshippers sent for them and invited them to enter his religion, but they refused. So he dug a trench, kindled a fire in it, and gave them the choice between entering his religion and being thrown into the fire. They chose being thrown into the fire over returning from their religion, and they were thrown in. Allah saved the believers who were thrown into the fire by taking their souls before the fire touched them, and the fire came out upon those of the disbelievers who were on the edge of the trench and burned them.

﴿While they sat over it, and they were witnesses to what they did to the believers﴾: witnesses, present. Muqatil said: meaning they bear witness that the believers, when they abandoned the worship of the idol, ﴿and they did not hold it against them﴾: that is, they found no fault in them, found no crime in them, and saw no wrong in them, ﴿except that they believed in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; and Allah is Witness over all things﴾. ﴿except that they believed﴾: meaning, except because and for the reason that they believed.

﴿Indeed, those who afflicted the believing men and believing women﴾: tortured and burned them. Its parallel is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿On the day they will be tried over the Fire﴾ [[Surat al-Dhariyat: 13.]], ﴿then they did not repent, so for them is the punishment of Hell﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and for them is the punishment of burning﴾ in this world. This is because Allah, Exalted is He, burned them with that same fire with which they had burned the believers. This is the statement of al-Rabi' and his companions. Others said: the two are one.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Lu'lu' al-Warraq told us, saying: Abu Ubayd Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Mu'ammal al-Sayrafi told us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Ahwal, known as al-Luqluq, told us, saying: Mansur ibn Ammar told us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Tawba told us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Jahm, traced back to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ confided to me a hadith about the Fire. He said: "O Hudhayfah, in Hell there are lions of fire, dogs of fire, hooks of fire, and swords of fire. Allah will send angels who will hang the people of the Fire by those hooks by their jaws, and cut them with those swords limb by limb, and throw them to those dogs and lions; whenever they cut off a limb, a new limb returns in its place." [123] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/174.]]

﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great triumph.﴾ The scholars differed regarding the response (jawab) of the oath. Some said: its response is ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾, and there is an omission in it, meaning: "Indeed, it was destroyed." It was also said: there is an inversion (taqdim and ta'khir), its intended sense being: ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench, by the sky of the constellations﴾.

Qatadah said: its response is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the seizing of your Lord is severe﴾, meaning His seizing with punishment and vengeance.

﴿Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats﴾: meaning, creation, according to most scholars. Ata al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿He originates﴾ the punishment in this world for the disbelievers, then ﴿repeats﴾ the punishment upon them in the Hereafter.

﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Loving﴾. Ibn Abbas said: His affection (tawaddud) toward His allies through forgiveness. Ali narrated from him: the Beloved. Mujahid: the Loving (al-Wadd). Ibn Zayd: the Merciful. It was also said: it is in the sense of the one loved (al-mawdud), like al-halub and al-rakub. It was also said: its meaning is that He forgives and loves to forgive.

﴿Lord of the Throne, the Glorious﴾: the great throne. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: the Generous. The reciters differed regarding it: Yahya, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read it with a kasra on the dal, as a descriptive (na't) of al-Arsh (the Throne). Others read it with a raf', as an attribute of al-Ghafur.

﴿Doer of what He intends﴾. ﴿Has there reached you the story of the hosts﴾: news of the destroyed armies. Then He specified who they were, saying:

﴿Pharaoh and Thamud﴾. ﴿But those who disbelieve are in denial﴾: from your people, O Muhammad. ﴿[And they submitted to torment]﴾ [[So in the manuscript.]], like the practice of those before them. ﴿And Allah, from behind them, is encompassing﴾: knowing of them, nothing of their conditions being hidden from Him. ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an﴾: noble, honorable, abundant in good, and not as the polytheists claimed. Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya said: "Majid" means uncreated.

Ibn al-Sumayqa read: ﴿Bal huwa Quranu majidin﴾ with idafa, meaning the Qur'an of a glorious Lord.

﴿In a preserved tablet﴾.

Yahya ibn Ya'mur read: ﴿fi luhin﴾ with a damma on the lam, meaning that it is in a tablet, and it is possessed of light, elevation and honor.

The others read it with a fatha on the lam, ﴿lawhin mahfuz﴾. Nafi' and Ibn Mikhzar read the dhal of ﴿mahfuzun﴾ with a damma as a descriptive of the Qur'an; the rest read it with a kasra as a descriptive of the tablet.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Makhlad told us, saying: Ibn Khalawayh told us, saying: Isma'il told us, saying: Ishaq ibn Bishr told us, saying: Muqatil and Ibn Jurayj informed me, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: At the head of the tablet is: "There is no god but Allah alone; His religion is Islam, and Muhammad is His servant and Messenger." Whoever believes in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, affirms His promise and follows His messengers, He will admit into Paradise. He said: The tablet is of white pearl, its length the distance between the heavens and the earth, its width the distance between east and west; its edges are of pearls and rubies, its covers are of red ruby, its pen is light, and its writing is a decree fastened to the Throne. Its origin is in the lap of an angel called Matriyun, protected from the devils. That is His saying: ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an in a preserved tablet﴾. For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in it, every day, are three hundred and sixty glances: He gives life and causes death, honors and humbles, and ﴿does what He wills﴾.

Aqil informed me that al-Mu'afa informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Amr ibn Ali told us, saying: I heard Qurrah ibn Sulayman say: Harb ibn Surayh told us, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhayb told us, from Anas ibn Malik, regarding His saying: ﴿It is a glorious Qur'an in a preserved tablet﴾. He said: The preserved tablet which Allah mentioned is on the forehead of Israfil. Muqatil said: The preserved tablet is to the right of the Throne.

**Qutila** (was cursed): Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Everything in the Qur'an that uses *qutila* means *la'ana* (was cursed)."

**Ashab al-Ukhdud** (the People of the Trench): *al-Shaqq* (the cleft). The scholars differed about them.

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Jaʿfar informed us, saying: al-Hakim Abu Muhammad Yahya ibn Mansur, and Abu al-Qasim Mansur ibn al-ʿAbbas (the sons of Shanj), and Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Mahmud ibn ʿUbayd Allah in Merv, and Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd Allah al-Tahiri [....] [[An illegible word in the manuscript.]], and the wording is his, said: Al-Hasan ibn Shaybān ibn ʿĀmir al-Shaybani narrated to us that Hudba ibn Khalid al-Qaysi narrated to them, saying: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, and I was told by Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Muhammad ibn Maʿmar narrated to me, who said: Harmi ibn ʿUmara narrated to me, who said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, who said: Thabit ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated to us, from Suhayb, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"There was a king among those before you, and he had a sorcerer. When the sorcerer grew old, he said to the king: 'I have grown old, so send me a boy to teach him sorcery.' So he sent him a boy to teach. On his way there was a monk, and the boy sat with him and heard his speech, and it pleased him. Whenever he came to the sorcerer, the sorcerer beat him, and whenever he returned from the sorcerer, he sat with the monk and heard his speech. When he came to his family, they beat him. He complained of this to the monk, who said: 'If you are detained by the sorcerer, say: "My family detained me." And if you are detained by your family, say: "The sorcerer detained me."' While he was in that state, he came upon a huge beast that had blocked the people. He said: 'Today I will know whether the sorcerer or the monk is better.' He took a stone and said: 'O Allah, if the affair of the monk is more beloved to You than the affair of the sorcerer, then kill this beast so the people may pass.' He threw it and killed it, and the people passed. He came to the monk and informed him. The monk said: 'My son, you are today better than me. Your affair has reached what I see, and you will be tested. When you are tested, do not point to me.' The boy used to heal the blind and the leper and treat people for all other ailments. A companion of the king, who had been blind, heard of him and brought him many gifts, saying: 'All this is yours if you cure me.' He said: 'I do not cure anyone; it is Allah, Mighty and Majestic, who cures. If you believe in Allah, I will supplicate Allah, and He will cure you.' So he believed in Allah, and Allah cured him. He came to the king walking and sat with him as he used to sit. The king said to him, and asked him: 'By what were you cured?' He said: 'By the supplication of the boy.' So the king sent for the boy and said: 'My son, your sorcery has reached the point that you cure the blind and the leper, and you do such and such.' He continued to torture him until he pointed to the monk. The monk was brought, and it was said to him: 'Return from your religion.' He refused. So he called for a saw, placed the saw at the parting of his head, and sawed him until his two halves fell. Then the boy was brought, and it was said to him: 'Return from your religion.' He refused. So he handed him over to a group of his companions and said to them: 'Take him to such-and-such mountain, climb with him, and when he reaches its peak, if he returns from his religion, well; otherwise, throw him down.' They took him, climbed the mountain with him, and he said: 'O Allah, suffice me against them however You wish.' The mountain shook beneath them and they fell. He came walking to the king, who said to him: 'What did your companions do?' He said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sufficed me against them.' So he handed him over to another group of his companions and said: 'Carry him in a small boat, take him to the middle of the sea, and if he returns from his religion, well; otherwise, cast him into it.'

They took him, and he said: 'O Allah, suffice me against them by whatever You wish.' The boat capsized with them, and they drowned. He came walking to the king, who said to him: 'What did your companions do?' He said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sufficed me against them.' Then he said to the king: 'You will not kill me until you do what I command you.' He said: 'What is it?' He said: 'Gather the people on one level plain, crucify me on a trunk, then take an arrow from my quiver, place the arrow in the middle of the bow, and say: "In the name of Allah, Lord of the boy," then shoot me. When you do that, you will kill me.' So he gathered the people on one level plain, crucified him on a trunk, took an arrow from his quiver, and placed the arrow at his temple. The boy placed his hand at the spot of the arrow and died. The people said:

'We believe in the Lord of the boy, we believe in the Lord of the boy,' three times each.

Then the king was approached and it was said to him: 'You have seen what you were wary of; by Allah, your wariness has come upon you. All the people have believed.' So he ordered [the digging of] the trench at the mouths of the streets, lit the fires, and said: 'Whoever does not return from his religion, throw him into it,' or it was said to him: 'Leap in.' They did that, until a woman came with a small child of hers, and she hesitated to fall into it. The boy said: 'O mother, be patient, for you are upon the truth.'" [122] [[Al-Ahad wa al-Mathani by al-Dahhak: 1/219–221, no. 187; and Sahih Muslim: 8/231.]]

Muhammad ibn Yahya said: Muslim ibn Qutayba narrated to us, who said: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from Ayyub, from ʿIkrima, concerning the saying of Allah, Glorified be He: ﴿Qutila ashab al-ukhdud﴾ (Cursed were the people of the trench). He said: "They were from your people, the Nabat." Al-Kalbi said: "They were Christians of Najran. The king of Najran seized believing people there, dug seven trenches for them in the ground, each forty cubits long and twelve cubits wide, then cast into them [naft] [[As in the manuscript.]] and firewood, then presented them to it. Whoever refused, they threw into the fire." He began with a man called ʿAmr ibn Zayd, and their king asked him: "Who taught you this?" meaning the tawhid (affirmation of Allah's oneness). He refused to tell him. So they brought the one who had taught him tawhid and said: "O king, I taught him." His name was ʿAbd Allah ibn Shamir, and he was thrown into the fire. Then they presented the believers to the fire one by one, until when he wanted to take the rest of the believers, their king made an idol of gold and appointed over every ten believers a man who would say to them: "When you hear the sound of the flutes, prostrate to the idol. Whoever does not prostrate, throw him into the fire." When the Christians heard of this, they prostrated to the idol, but the believers refused. So he dug trenches for them and threw them in, and the fire rose above them twelve cubits.

Muqatil said: "The trenches were three: one in Najran in Yemen, another in Syria, and another in Persia, where they were burned with fire. As for the one in Syria, it was Antiochus ibn Maysar the Roman; as for the one in Persia, it was Bukhtnassar; and as for the one in the land of the Arabs, it was Yusuf ibn Dhi Nuwas. Allah did not send down a Qur'an concerning those in Persia and Syria, but He sent down concerning the one in Najran. That was because two Muslim men, of those who read the Gospel, one in the land of Tihama and the other in Najran of Yemen, one of them hired himself out for a job and began reading the Gospel. The daughter of his employer saw a light shining while he was reading the Gospel, and she told her father of it. He watched him until he saw it, and asked him, but he did not inform him. He kept at him until he informed him of the religion and Islam. So he (the employer) and eighty-seven persons, men and women, followed him, and this was after ʿIsa had been raised to heaven. Yusuf ibn Dhi Nuwas ibn Sharahil ibn Tubba' ibn al-Yasuh al-Himyari heard of that, dug trenches for them in the ground, lit fires in them, and presented them with disbelief. Whoever refused to disbelieve, he threw into the fire, and whoever returned from the religion of ʿIsa was not thrown into the fire. A woman came with a small child who could not speak. When she stood at the edge of the trench, she looked at her son and drew back from the fire. She was struck until she moved forward, and she continued like that three times. When it was the third time, she went to turn back, and her son said to her: 'O mother, I see before you a fire that will not be extinguished.' When she heard her son say that, they both threw themselves into the fire together, and Allah made her and her son to be in Paradise. On that single day, seventy-seven persons were thrown into the fire."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Whoever refused to fall into the fire was beaten with whips, and their spirits were admitted into Paradise before their bodies reached the fire."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih that a man who had remained upon the religion of ʿIsa came to Najran and invited them, and they answered him. Dhu Nuwas the Jew marched against him with troops from Himyar and gave them the choice between the fire and Judaism. They refused him, so he dug the trenches and burned twelve thousand. Al-Kalbi said: "The People of the Trench were seventy thousand."

Wahb said: "When Abraha overcame Yemen, Dhu Nuwas fled and plunged into the sea with his horse, and drowned." In this regard ʿAmr ibn Maʿdi Karib said:

"You threaten me as if you were Dhu Ruʿayn,
or Dhu Nuwas in his most pleasant life.
Before you there were blessings and a kingdom firmly established among people,
ancient its covenant, from whose covenant was ʿAd,
great, conqueror of tyranny, harsh.
Time removed their kingship, and it became
transferred among people from people."

Al-Kalbi said: "Dhu Nuwas is the one who killed ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Tamir, and the story has already passed in the raised (marfuʿ) hadith to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." Something that makes it clearer is what ʿAta' narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he said: "In Najran there was a king from the kings of Himyar called Yusuf Dhu Nuwas ibn Sharahbil ibn Sharahil, in the interval before the birth of the Prophet (ﷺ) by ninety years."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn Muhammad ibn Bahir narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Humayd al-Kashshi narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, who said: Yaʿqub ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Qummi narrated to us, who said: Jaʿfar ibn Abi al-Mughira narrated to us, from Ibn [Abzi], who said: "When the Muslims defeated the people of Isfandhan, they turned back, and he (ʿUmar) came to them, and they gathered. They said: 'What rulings apply to the Magians? They are not People of the Book, nor are they among the polytheist Arabs.' ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said: 'Rather, they are People of the Book, and they were adhering to their scripture. Wine had been made lawful for them. A king of theirs took it and it overpowered his mind, so he had relations with his sister. When the intoxication left him, he regretted and said to her: "Woe to you, what is this that I have done, and what is the way out of it?"

She said: "The way out is that you address the people, saying: 'O people, Allah has made lawful the marriage of sisters.' When it has departed from the people and they forget it, then you address them and forbid it."

So he stood as a preacher and said: "O people, Allah has made lawful the marriage of sisters." The people, all of them, said: "God forbid that we believe in this or acknowledge it. No prophet has brought it to us, nor was it sent down to us in a book." He returned to his partner and said: "Woe to you, the people have refused me." She said: "If they refuse you, then spread the whip among them." He said: "So he spread the whip among them, but the people refused to acknowledge it." He returned to her and said: "I have spread the whip among them, and they refused to acknowledge it." She said: "Then draw the sword against them." He said: "So he drew the sword against them, but they refused to acknowledge it." He said to her: "Woe to you, the people have refused to acknowledge it." She said: "Dig for them a trench, then light fires in it, then present to it the people of your kingdom. Whoever follows you, leave him alone; and whoever refuses, throw him into the fire." So he dug a trench for them, lit fires in it, and presented the people of his realm to that. Whoever refused was thrown into the fire, and whoever agreed was let go." So Allah, Glorified be He, sent down concerning them: ﴿Qutila ashab al-ukhdud. The fire full of fuel﴾ up to His saying: ﴿ʿadhab al-hariq﴾ (the punishment of the burning) [[Tafsir al-Tabari with slight variation: 30/166.]].

Al-Dahhak said: "The People of the Trench were from the Children of Israel. They seized men and women, dug a trench for them, then lit fires in it and made the believers stand over it, saying: 'Will you disbelieve, or shall we throw you into the fire?' They claim that they were Daniel and his companions." This is the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, who said: ʿUmar ibn Muhammad ibn Bahir narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Yunus, from Shayban, from Qatada, concerning the saying of Allah, Glorified be He: ﴿Qutila ashab al-ukhdud﴾. He said: "[Someone] narrated to us that ʿAli ibn Abi Talib used to say: 'They were people in Mudra' of Yemen. Their believers fought their disbelievers, and the believers prevailed over the disbelievers. Then they fought a second time, and the believers prevailed over the disbelievers. Then they took covenants and pledges from one another that none would betray another. But their disbelievers betrayed them and seized them. Then a man from among the believers said to them: "Is there for you some good? Kindle a fire, then present us to it. Whoever follows you in your religion, that is what you desire; and whoever does not, let him leap into the fire, and you will be rid of him." So they kindled a fire and presented them to it, and they began to leap into it, until only an old woman remained, as if she hesitated. A small child in her lap said to her: "Go on, and do not hesitate." So Allah related to them their news and their story."

ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid also informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Muzani informed us, who said: Mutayn narrated to us, who said: ʿUthman narrated to us, who said: Muʿawiya ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Sharik, from Jabir, from Abu al-Tufayl, from ʿAli, who said: "The People of the Trench, their prophet was Abyssinian." ʿAli said: "A prophet from Abyssinia was sent to his people." Then he recited to me: ﴿Wa-laqad arsalna rusulan min qablika minhum man qasasna ʿalayka wa-minhum man lam naqsus ʿalayka﴾ (And We certainly sent messengers before you; of them are those We have related to you, and of them are those We have not related to you) [[Surah Ghafir 40:78.]]. The prophet invited them, and some people followed him. They fought them, and his companions were killed, and he was seized and bound, but he escaped from them. They dug a trench and filled it with fire. Whoever followed the prophet was thrown into it, and whoever followed them was left alone. Then they brought a woman with a suckling child, and she recoiled. He said: "O mother, go on and do not hesitate." [[The same source, in which: "go on and do not wail."]]

And through him, from Mutayn, who said: Abu Musa narrated to us, and he said: "In their land there was a boy called ʿAbd Allah ibn Tamir. His father had handed him over to a teacher to teach him sorcery. The boy disliked that and found no escape from obeying his father, so he kept going to the teacher. On his way there was a monk of beautiful recitation and beautiful voice, which pleased him. He would come to the teacher after the other boys, and the teacher would beat him, saying: 'What detained you?' When he returned to his father, he entered upon the monk, and his father beat him, saying: 'Why were you late?' So the boy complained of this to the monk, who said to him: 'When you come to the teacher, say: "My father detained me." And when you come to your father, say: "The teacher detained me."'

In that land there was a huge serpent that cut off the road for the people. The boy passed by it, threw at it, and killed it. The monk learned of this and was all the more amazed by him, and said: 'You killed it?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'You have a great affair.'

The king had a son who was blind. He heard about the boy and that he had killed the serpent, so he came to him with an attendant and said: 'Did you kill the serpent?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Who killed it?' He said: 'Allah.' He said: 'Who is Allah?' He said: 'Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, and Lord of the sun, the moon, the night and the day, and this world and the Hereafter.' He said: 'If you are truthful, then supplicate your Lord that He return my sight to me.' The boy said: 'Do you see? If Allah returns your sight to you, will you believe in Him?' He said: 'Yes.' The boy said: 'O Allah, if he is truthful, return his sight to him.' Allah, Exalted, returned his sight to him, and he went back to his home without an attendant. Then he entered upon the king, and when the king saw him, he was amazed and said: 'Who did this?' He said: 'Allah.' He said: 'And who is Allah?' He said: 'Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, Lord of the East and the West, Lord of the sun, the moon, the night and the day, and this world and the Hereafter.' The king said to him: 'Tell me, who taught you this?' and he pointed to the boy. He called him and spoke with him, and he was an intelligent boy. He asked him about his religion, and the boy informed him of Islam and of those who believed with him. The king resolved to kill them, fearing that they would change his religion. So he sent them to the top of a mountain and said: 'Throw them from the top of the mountain.' They took the boy to the highest mountain, and the boy supplicated his Lord, and Allah destroyed them. This angered the king. Then he sent men with them to the sea and said: 'Drown them.' The boy supplicated his Lord, and He drowned them, and he and his companions were saved. He entered upon the king, who said: 'What did your companions do, those whom I sent with you?' He said: 'Allah destroyed them and saved me.' He said: 'Kill him with the sword.' But the sword turned away from him. His news spread in the land of Yemen, and people knew him and magnified him, and they knew that he and his companions were upon the truth. The boy said to the king: 'You will not be able to kill me unless you do what I tell you.' He said: 'How shall I kill you?' He said: 'Gather the people of your kingdom while you are on your throne, then shoot me with an arrow in the name of my God.' The king did so, then he shot him in the name of the boy's God, and it struck him and killed him. The people said:"

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 85, verse 4–22 (part 2 of 2):

There is no god but Allah, the Lord of Abdullah ibn Thamir, and there is no religion but his religion." The king became angry, closed the door, seized the mouths of the lanes, and dug a trench (ukhdud) and filled it with fire. Then he presented them to himself man by man: whoever turned back from Islam he left alone, and whoever said, "My religion is the religion of Abdullah," he threw into the trench and burned him. In his kingdom there was a woman who had embraced Islam along with those who embraced it, and she had three children, one of whom was an infant. The king said to her, "Return from your religion, or I will throw you into the fire and your children with you." She refused, so he took her eldest son and threw him into the fire. Then he said to her, "Return to your religion," and she refused, so he threw the second into the fire. Then he said to her, "Return from your religion," and she refused. They took the child from her to throw him into the fire, and the woman was about to turn back, but the child said, "O mother, do not turn back from Islam, for you are upon the truth and there is no harm upon you." The child was thrown into the fire, and his mother was thrown after him. This is the meaning of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench﴾ [[With variation from the tafsir of al-Qurtubi: 19/289.]].

And al-Dahhak said: Bukhtnassar burned a group of the Muslims.

Al-ukhdud: the pit, and the long cleft in the earth like a river; its plural is akhadid. It is on the pattern of af'ul from al-khadd; one says "khaddadtu fi al-ard khaddan," meaning I cut and dug.

﴿The fire fueled with wood﴾: the common reading is with a fatha on the waw, meaning the fuel (al-khatb). Abu Raja' al-Utaridi read it with a damma on the waw, as a verbal noun (masdar). The common reading of ﴿nari dhat﴾ is with a kasra, so both are in apposition (na't) to al-ukhdud. Ashhab al-Uqayli read it with a raf' in both, meaning: ﴿the fire fueled with wood﴾ burned them.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The people of the trench were a group of believers who had withdrawn from people during a period of interruption (fatra). A tyrant of the idol-worshippers sent for them and invited them to enter his religion, but they refused. So he dug a trench, kindled a fire in it, and gave them the choice between entering his religion and being thrown into the fire. They chose being thrown into the fire over returning from their religion, and they were thrown in. Allah saved the believers who were thrown into the fire by taking their souls before the fire touched them, and the fire came out upon those of the disbelievers who were on the edge of the trench and burned them.

﴿While they sat over it, and they were witnesses to what they did to the believers﴾: witnesses, present. Muqatil said: meaning they bear witness that the believers, when they abandoned the worship of the idol, ﴿and they did not hold it against them﴾: that is, they found no fault in them, found no crime in them, and saw no wrong in them, ﴿except that they believed in Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; and Allah is Witness over all things﴾. ﴿except that they believed﴾: meaning, except because and for the reason that they believed.

﴿Indeed, those who afflicted the believing men and believing women﴾: tortured and burned them. Its parallel is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿On the day they will be tried over the Fire﴾ [[Surat al-Dhariyat: 13.]], ﴿then they did not repent, so for them is the punishment of Hell﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and for them is the punishment of burning﴾ in this world. This is because Allah, Exalted is He, burned them with that same fire with which they had burned the believers. This is the statement of al-Rabi' and his companions. Others said: the two are one.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Lu'lu' al-Warraq told us, saying: Abu Ubayd Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Mu'ammal al-Sayrafi told us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Ahwal, known as al-Luqluq, told us, saying: Mansur ibn Ammar told us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Tawba told us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Jahm, traced back to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ confided to me a hadith about the Fire. He said: "O Hudhayfah, in Hell there are lions of fire, dogs of fire, hooks of fire, and swords of fire. Allah will send angels who will hang the people of the Fire by those hooks by their jaws, and cut them with those swords limb by limb, and throw them to those dogs and lions; whenever they cut off a limb, a new limb returns in its place." [123] [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/174.]]

﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great triumph.﴾ The scholars differed regarding the response (jawab) of the oath.
